# Doing: the cycle record

What is being done: the running cycle's planning and its work's documentation. The last
finished cycle's is in [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md), and what we might do is in [TODO.md](TODO.md). The
block's shape is on trial: it opens with the Todo as it was picked from `TODO.md`, then the
Deliberation, the plan, Solution and Acceptance check, and the Ladder with its details.

This file is a trial (2026-10-09). The agent-files still name `TODO.md > ## In Progress` as the
record's home, and the cycle that makes this file the rule is [The cycle-record moves out of
TODO.md into zDOING.md](TODO.md#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record: read first, acted
on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader. Kept here by the trial, with a pointer to it under the
same heading in `TODO.md`, where [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) still looks.

_None._

## In Progress

### docs: the session lock is settled as flock

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) The Todo as it was picked, **The lock a running agent holds**, less
its plan for `.vc-x1-running`, which stays in `## Todo` as an entry of its own. The file is
`.agent-running` at the workspace root, in `.gitignore`. It is a mutex a running agent holds, one
session per workspace, and a second session that finds it held refuses to work. The entry ended
on an open line: whether the lock is a counter, the `flock`, or a counter guarded by one.

- Wink's first design: the file holds a counter, a session adds one and takes one away, and the
  file is deleted at 0.
  - The update is a read, change, and write that two sessions starting together can interleave,
    so it wants a guard.
  - A session that dies never takes its one away, and a number does not say which holder is dead.
- Linux's advisory lock, `flock`, answers both: the kernel releases it when its holder exits or
  dies. The file then has no contents and is never deleted.
  - The first form was shared: each session held it shared, and rename and delete asked for it
    exclusive without waiting. A second session then started as freely as the first.
  - Wink's call, 2026-10-11: one session per workspace. The session holds it exclusive and asks
    without waiting, so a second session's request fails at once instead of queueing.
  - It is advisory: it binds the processes that ask. Claude Code itself still starts, and the
    refusal is the agent's, by the `custom.md` line.
  - The lock lasts as long as the process holding it, and an agent's commands each exit at once,
    so a session needs one process that lives exactly as long as it does.
- The experiment: the agent takes the lock at acquaint, by a line in this project's `custom.md`,
  which [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) already reads and acts on.
  - The holder is a background command the agent starts, `flock -xn .agent-running sleep
    infinity`, so there is no release for the agent to forget.
  - A foreground probe comes first, `flock -xn .agent-running true`, since a background command
    reports its failure seconds later, after the session has moved on.
  - A refusal is one fixed sentence, so the session offers no way around the lock.
  - The check is `flock -xn .agent-running true` from another terminal: it fails while a session
    is open and succeeds after.
- What the experiment was to find out: whether the holder dies with its session, what a resumed
  session does, what a reacquaint does in a session that no longer remembers its holder, how an
  edit to the line reaches a session already open, and how rename and delete check.

#### Deliberation

- The lock is the `flock`, exclusive, and no counter, wink's call once the tests were in.
  - Every way a session ends releases it, so nothing is left for a counter to count.
  - The tests came before the cycle was opened, wink's call, each of them ending the session
    that would have reported it.
- The holder dies with its session, however the session ends.
  - A clean exit: a session was ended with `/exit`, and the next session's probe succeeded.
    Claude Code asks before that exit, the holder being a background command still running, and
    exiting anyway kills it. The question is one more key at every exit.
  - A crash: wink's check from a plain terminal exited 1 with a session open, Claude Code was
    killed with `kill -9`, and the check exited 0 twenty seconds later.
  - A closed terminal: the check exited 1 with the session open and 0 after its terminal
    window was closed.
  - Each session ran its commands in Claude Code's sandbox. One run outside it is untested, and
    we think it is the same, the kernel releasing a lock when the last process holding it dies.
- A resumed session holds no lock, and the line now tells it to take one.
  - The session the closed terminal ended was resumed with `claude --resume`, and the check
    from a plain terminal still exited 0.
  - Claude Code tells the resumed session that its holder was stopped when the earlier process
    exited, and starts nothing in its place.
  - The line as it was gave that case the refusal sentence and the stop, the holder having
    exited, and the sentence would have been untrue, no other session holding the lock.
  - The session ran no command until wink said to take the lock again.
  - "If that command ever exits" became "exits while the session runs", so the two cases do not
    read as one.
- The probe run by the session that holds the lock exits 1, confirmed by running it.
  - A reacquaint in a session that no longer remembers its holder would read that as another
    session and stop. The line's "a session that already holds one does neither" is all that
    stands against it, and the case goes to the `.vc-x1-running` entry with the hook command.
- The link at the end of the lock line is dropped, the entry it named being this record.
- The `.vc-x1-running` plan is an entry of its own, first in `## Todo`, wink's call.
  - It takes what the session lock leaves: the hook command, the reacquaint cases, and the
    proposal of the lock to the set.
  - It answers how rename and delete check, the process that asks being the process that
    holds.
- The cycle is two stages and one work commit, wink's call, as the last two cycles ran.
  - It bends [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape), [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record),
    [Opening](AGENTS.md#opening), and [Close-out](AGENTS.md#close-out) as the record in the
    landmark `docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md` says, the record kept in this file
    included.
  - The fold of the closing into the work commit is by hand again, `push --amend` not being
    written, and is a coordinated re-describe with one trailer written by hand.
  - The bend covers this cycle's two pushes and their shape. Land takes its own go.
- The title was counted before the bookmark was published, 42 characters, and both were
  approved by wink at the opening.
- The `## Waiting` conditions are unmet, `vc-x1 closed` not landed and jj-lib offering no remote
  query, so nothing promotes.

#### Solution

Provisional: the session lock is recorded as finished, and what is left is planned elsewhere.

- The lock line in `custom.md` loses its link and gains the resumed session's case.
- The Todo entry becomes this record, with the four results and `flock`, exclusive, as the
  answer to its open line.
- The `.vc-x1-running` plan stands alone as the first entry in `## Todo`.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate` passes.
- A session that met the new line cold takes the lock again when resumed: a fresh session is
  started and acquaints, its terminal is closed, it is resumed and sent one message, and its
  transcript shows the probe and the holder as its first two commands. The check from a plain
  terminal then exits 1.

#### Ladder

- docs: the session lock is settled as flock (done)

# References

lines: killed with `kill -9`, and the check exited 0 twenty seconds later.
- A closed terminal: the check exited 1 with the session open and 0 after its terminal
window was closed.
+  - A power loss: wink's pull-the-plug test, 2026-10-11, with a session open. With the machine
+    back up the check exited 0, `.agent-running` was still there and empty, and `vc-x1 sync` and
+    `vc-x1 st -s both` found both repos up to date and clean.
- Each session ran its commands in Claude Code's sandbox. One run outside it is untested, and
we think it is the same, the kernel releasing a lock when the last process holding it dies.
- A resumed session holds no lock, and the line now tells it to take one.

vc-x1 0.84.23

Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes.

Repo set is resolved (in order):
  - `-R` / `--repo`     exact list (back-compat / arbitrary multi-repo)
  - `--scope=work|agent|work,agent` dual-repo roles via `.vc-config.toml`
  - neither             `.`, the one repo sync is run in

Safe by default: before it fetches, sync finds out what the
fetch would do. It asks the remote where its bookmarks are,
downloads the commits of those that moved without moving a
ref, and tells a fast-forward from a rewrite. Then:
  - remote has not moved   nothing to fetch
  - only fast-forwarded    fetch; local work is left untouched
  - would tangle           held back; sync says why, exits non-zero
A fetch would tangle local work when a bookmark that moved has
local commits of its own, or when the remote rewrote a
bookmark and the repo holds local work: uncommitted changes in
`@` (not asked of the agent repo, whose `@` holds the running
session), an `@-` that is not on the remote, or a bookmark
with commits the remote does not have. --force, or --rebase,
syncs a repo that would be held back.

With --dry-run sync does the same finding out and stops: it
reports each repo's state, its local work, and what a sync
would do, and moves no bookmark, `@`, or remote-tracking ref.
It exits 0 whatever it finds.

One atomic operation: fetch, then per repo, by where its
bookmark was before the fetch:
  - up-to-date        nothing to do
  - behind            fast-forward bookmark to remote
  - rewritten         the remote replaced the commit; fetch followed it
  - ahead             nothing to sync
  - diverged          --force only: rebase onto remote, fail on conflicts
  - no remote         bookmark has no @<remote> counterpart; skip

After a successful sync, `@` is repositioned onto the synced
bookmark: the work repo `jj new`s a clean `@` (or with
--force rebases a dirty one), the `.claude` session repo
`jj new main`s when main moved (no-op when `@-` is already
the main tip).

On failure sync stops where the failing step stopped: nothing
is auto-reverted, so the state can be inspected. The failure
report prints each repo's pre-sync op id; undo explicitly with
`jj op restore <op> -R <repo>`. Nothing persists across
invocations.

Output shape:
  - all-up-to-date: one-line summary (`sync: N repos are up to date, nothing to
  sync`)
  - anything else:  per-repo fetch + state + actions
  - --quiet:        no output; exit code signals success

Usage: vc-x1 sync [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -q, --quiet
          Suppress all informational output (exit code signals result)

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to sync in the work repo. The session (bot) repo is a linear
          journal and always syncs `main`, regardless
          
          [default: main]

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --remote <REMOTE>
          Remote to sync against
          
          [default: origin]

      --force
          Sync a repo even where sync would hold it back, rebasing what the sync
          needs rebased. `--rebase` is the same flag.
          
          Sync holds a repo back when what the remote did would tangle local
          work: a bookmark that moved on the remote has local commits of its
          own, or the remote rewrote a bookmark and the repo holds local work.
          With `--force` the repo is fetched all the same, a diverged bookmark
          is rebased onto its remote, and a work repo `@` that carries changes
          onto the synced bookmark. The bot repo's `@` is never rebased (it
          always `jj new main`).
          
          [alias: --rebase]

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --dry-run
          Look only: report each repo's local work and where it stands against
          its remote, and change nothing.
          
          Nothing is fetched. The remote is asked which commit its bookmarks
          are, the commits of those that moved are downloaded with no ref moved,
          and the report says what a sync would do: nothing, follow the remote,
          or be held back and why. Exits 0 whenever the look itself succeeded,
          whatever it found.

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Workspace root, or a single jj repo to sync on its own.
          
          - `-R PATH` alone: sync just the repo at PATH.
          - `-R PATH -s ROLES`: use PATH as the workspace root and
            sync the named side(s).

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repo(s) of the workspace to sync.
          
          `SCOPE=work|agent|both`:
          
          - `work`: sync only the work repo.
          - `agent`: sync only the bot repo (errors if no bot repo
            is configured).
          - `both` (or `work,agent`): sync both repos.
          
          Composes with `-R` as the workspace root. With neither,
          sync acts on `.`, the one repo it is run in.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

The pull-the-plug result is in `zDOING.md`, as a fourth item under "The holder dies with its session"; it is uncommitted in `@` and rides with the closing fold.

## What v028 is

`agent-filesproposal-v028` is one commit from 2026-10-09, `2b14ec7e`, sitting on `cf527955` "feat: bare sync acts on the repo it is run in". `main` has moved seven commits past that point. It carries three rule changes:

- **Acquaint, Not level:** the `jj git fetch` and a look becomes `vc-x1 sync --scope=both`, which fetches and brings each `main` level. "Left as found" gains "the sync's own acts aside", and the cycle's bookmark is still only compared.
- **Opening, new step 1:** "every cycle start syncs, whatever its form", ahead of the bookmark. The other steps renumber to 2 through 6.
- **`custom.md`:** the messages repo is fetched at acquaint and at every cycle start, with your standing permission dated 2026-10-09.

Alongside those it has the two rationale paragraphs, the size row (1802 to 1809), the `agent-files-v0.2.8` marker, and its own closed record.

## What has gone stale

- **Its wait is over.** It parked on `sync --dry-run`, which landed in `f69a8843`, and sync is now safe by default.
- **The wording describes the old sync.** It says a `main` that diverged is rebased before you hear of it. Today's sync holds that repo back and exits non-zero unless given `--force`. The "what it costs" rationale paragraph and "the sync's own acts aside" are mostly moot.
- **The two steps can now look first.** The commit's own Todo entry planned a one-line follow-up pointing Acquaint and Opening at `--dry-run`. That can be folded in now, so "left as found" holds with no exception.
- **Version and name.** It has `vc-x1-dev` at `0.84.21`, while `main` is at `0.84.23`. Agent-files v0.2.8 is still unclaimed.
- **`TODO.md` will conflict.**
  - Its "sync has a look-only mode" entry is already done.
  - Its `zDOING.md` entry is superseded by the trial.
  - Its closed record sits in `## Closed`, where `main` now uses `zCLOSED.md`.
  - "TODO.md is renamed zTODO.md" is the one entry I have not checked against `main`.
- **`custom.md` will conflict lightly**, since the Lock line now sits above Messaging.
- **Its title is wrong on one point.** It says "local, unpushed", but the bookmark is on `origin`.

## Recommendation

Do not rebase it. Run it as a fresh `agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8` cycle on current `main` after the flock cycle lands, carrying the three rules over by hand and rewording them for today's sync. Then delete the parked bookmark locally and on `origin`, with your go for the remote delete.

Decision for you: should Acquaint and Opening run `vc-x1 sync --dry-run --scope=both` and report, or run the real sync? I would use the dry run at Acquaint and the real sync at Opening, since an opening wants `main` level before the bookmark is created.

The plain version: v028 is a small rule change to sync at acquaint and at every cycle start. The sync it was written for has since become safe and gained a look-only mode, so it needs rewording more than rebasing.

58	
59	### vc-x1 takes a lock of its own for every run
60	
61	(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) Two `vc-x1` runs in one workspace can overlap, a user's two terminals
62	included, and nothing serializes them. The session lock, `.agent-running`, keeps a second agent
63	session out of a workspace and says nothing about a run a user starts beside one.
64	
65	- The lock is `.vc-x1-running` at the workspace root, wink's thought: `vc-x1` takes it itself,
66	  exclusive and without waiting, for as long as one run lasts, so two runs in one workspace
67	  cannot overlap, whoever started them.
68	  - The process that asks is the process that holds, so a session's own `vc-x1` commands never
69	    collide with the session's holder.
70	  - That answers how rename and delete check: they take this lock and never ask for the
71	    session's, which the session running them already holds.
72	- It guards a run and nothing between runs. Two agents editing one working copy share one `@`,
73	  and a push takes the working copy whole, so one agent's edits land in the other's commit
74	  even when they touch different files. That is what `.agent-running` is for.
75	- So both, we think: `.vc-x1-running` for the run, `.agent-running` for the session, one agent
76	  per workspace, and a second agent gets a second clone.
77	- Every invocation takes it, wink's call, 2026-10-11, the simplest rule. Letting the ones that
78	  only read run beside another is a bridge crossed when it is wanted.
79	- To settle in its cycle: a run with no workspace yet (`init`, `clone`, `--help`) has no root to
80	  lock, and a `vc-x1` that starts another `vc-x1` in the same workspace would refuse itself.
81	- Left by the session lock, whose record is the landmark `docs: the session lock is settled as
82	  flock`:
83	  - A `vc-x1` command that takes and releases the session lock, for a session hook to call, so
84	    the lock no longer rests on a line the agent reads.
85	  - A reacquaint in a session that no longer remembers its holder probes, collides with its own
86	    holder, and reads that as another session.
87	  - A reacquaint does not always read `custom.md` again, so an edit to the lock line reaches a
88	    fresh session alone.
89	  - The session lock is proposed for the set by this entry's cycle, we think, `flock` being a
90	    Linux tool and the line being this project's.
91

### vc-x1 takes a lock of its own for every run

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) Two `vc-x1` runs in one workspace can overlap, a user's two terminals
included, and nothing serializes them. The session lock, `.agent-running`, keeps a second agent
session out of a workspace and says nothing about a run a user starts beside one.

- The lock is `.vc-x1-running` at the workspace root, wink's thought: `vc-x1` takes it itself,
  exclusive and without waiting, for as long as one run lasts, so two runs in one workspace
  cannot overlap, whoever started them.
  - The process that asks is the process that holds, so a session's own `vc-x1` commands never
    collide with the session's holder.
  - That answers how rename and delete check: they take this lock and never ask for the
    session's, which the session running them already holds.
- It guards a run and nothing between runs. Two agents editing one working copy share one `@`,
  and a push takes the working copy whole, so one agent's edits land in the other's commit
  even when they touch different files. That is what `.agent-running` is for.
- So both, we think: `.vc-x1-running` for the run, `.agent-running` for the session, one agent
  per workspace, and a second agent gets a second clone.
- Every invocation takes it, wink's call, 2026-10-11, the simplest rule. Letting the ones that
  only read run beside another is a bridge crossed when it is wanted.
- To settle in its cycle: a run with no workspace yet (`init`, `clone`, `--help`) has no root to
  lock, and a `vc-x1` that starts another `vc-x1` in the same workspace would refuse itself.
- Left by the session lock, whose record is the landmark `docs: the session lock is settled as
  flock`:
  - A `vc-x1` command that takes and releases the session lock, for a session hook to call, so
    the lock no longer rests on a line the agent reads.
  - A reacquaint in a session that no longer remembers its holder probes, collides with its own
    holder, and reads that as another session.
  - A reacquaint does not always read `custom.md` again, so an edit to the lock line reaches a
    fresh session alone.
  - The session lock is proposed for the set by this entry's cycle, we think, `flock` being a
    Linux tool and the line being this project's.

### push --amend folds a stage into the pushed work commit

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A cycle's closing wants to add to the work commit already pushed, not
to make a second one, and `vc-x1 push` can only make a new commit on each side. The cycle
**docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md** did it by hand: a `jj squash`, a `jj describe`
with a trailer written by hand, and then the push.

content.text:
Yes. "Opening" here is the Opening section of the cycle protocol: the moment a `## Todo` entry is picked and its cycle starts, before the cycle's bookmark is created. The parked text says "every cycle start syncs, whatever its form", so it covers an opening commit, a lightweight cycle's first commit, and a single-step cycle's one commit.

So the two steps would be:

- **Acquaint:** `vc-x1 sync --scope=both --dry-run`, once per session, which reports and moves nothing.
- **Opening:** `vc-x1 sync --scope=both`, once per cycle, as its first step, which brings each `main` level before the bookmark goes on it.

It is not run again at each rung or at the close-out, only at the start of a cycle. It syncs both repos each time, though the cycle's bookmark is in the work-repo only.

content.text:
Yes, I think Land should check too, and it is the one place where the check guards a shared target rather than a private bookmark.

- **What happens today without it:** the `main` push at Land is refused when the remote's `main` has moved, so nothing is lost. But it is found out last, after the reshape has built the merge commit and the artifact name has been restored, and that all has to be unpicked.
- **Where it goes:** first in Land, before the reshape. I would use the real sync there, as at Opening. Local `main` has no commits of its own before Land, so the sync can only fast-forward it, and the reshape then builds on a level `main`.
- **A moved `main` is a stop, not an automatic rebase.** What would land is no longer the tree you reviewed and validated.
  - *Version:* both cycles bumped from the same version-of-record, so the later lander needs a new number even when nothing conflicts textually.
  - *Shared files:* `TODO.md`, `zDOING.md` and `zCLOSED.md` are edited by every cycle, so two cycles will almost always conflict there.
  - *Validation:* it has to run again on the combined tree before the push.
- **The trapezoid softens the rebase question.** Its merge commit takes the trunk as first parent and the ladder as second, so a moved `main` can become the first parent without rewriting the pushed rungs. A single-step commit or a kept-separate ladder has no merge, so it needs a real rebase, which rewrites a published bookmark.
- **Opening's sync still earns its place.** It does not close the race, but it shortens the window from "since the session's acquaint" to "since this cycle began", which makes a moved `main` at Land rare and small.
- **The agent-repo is a different case.** Its `main` is pushed at every rung with no bookmark, so a second writer would collide at each push, not only at Land. The one-session lock covers this on one machine; a second machine is not covered by anything here.

If you take it, it belongs in the v0.2.8 entry as a third step beside Acquaint and Opening, with "a moved `main` at Land stops and asks" as the rule. How to recover from one could be left to the first time it happens.

The plain version: check `main` right before landing as well, because that is the only moment someone else can have got there first, and treat "they did" as a reason to stop and re-validate rather than something to fix automatically.

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### docs: a session takes the workspace lock at acquaint

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) Two agent sessions started in one workspace share one working copy,
and a push takes the working copy whole, so one session's edits land in the other's commit even
when the two touch different files. Nothing told a second session that a first was running.

#### Deliberation

- The lock is exclusive, one session per workspace, wink's call.
  - It was first taken shared, with rename and delete to ask for it exclusive. A second session
    then started as freely as the first, which is what the lock was wanted to stop.
  - A user who wants two agents at once makes a second clone.
- A foreground probe comes before the holder, `flock -xn .agent-running true`.
  - The holder is a background command, and its failure is reported seconds after it starts.
    The first trial session fetched both repos in that time.
  - The second trial session, told to confirm its holder was running, searched for it with
    `pgrep`, which sees only its own sandbox and printed the sandbox's command line.
  - Two sessions starting in the same second can both pass the probe. The loser's holder then
    exits, and the line gives that exit the same stop.
- A refusal is one fixed sentence, and no command follows it.
  - "Reports that" drew a summary, a suggested `lslocks`, and an offer to go on without the lock,
    which Claude Code turned into a one-key suggested prompt.
  - "Does nothing further" was read as nothing further of the acquaint: the next session still
    ran `ps` to find the holder. "Runs no further command, not even to find the holder" closed it.
- It is a rule of this project's `custom.md` and no `agent-files` proposal, wink's call.
  - A rule meant for the set belongs in [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint), and this one is not
    ready for other adopters: `flock` is a Linux tool, and two cases are untested, below.
  - The number v0.2.8 is the parked proposal's. We think the lock is proposed by the cycle that
    has `vc-x1` take a lock of its own.
- The Todo entry [The lock a running agent holds](TODO.md#the-lock-a-running-agent-holds) was not
  moved here. Most of it is still to do, `.vc-x1-running` first, so the block opens with the
  problem and the entry stays first in `## Todo`, where wink moved it.
- Two cases are left to that entry, untested: whether the holder dies with its session, which
  ends the session that would report it, and what a reacquaint does in the session that holds
  the lock.
- A reacquaint does not always read `custom.md` again. Two trial sessions skipped the read, so an
  edit to the line reached only a fresh session. It is a line in the Todo entry.
- The title is 53 characters, over the cap in [Line widths](agent-data/prose.md#line-widths),
  wink's call when the agent's count came after the bookmark was published. The bend covers
  this cycle's title alone.
- The cycle is two stages and one work commit, the shape the last cycle tried, wink's call.
  - It bends [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape), [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record),
    [Opening](AGENTS.md#opening), and [Close-out](AGENTS.md#close-out) as that cycle's record
    says, in the landmark `docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md`, the record kept in
    `zDOING.md` included.
  - The fold of the closing into the work commit is by hand again, `push --amend` not being
    written, and is a coordinated re-describe with one trailer written by hand.
- The bookmark's create and publish was approved by wink at the opening.
- The size table's new column is labelled `v0.2.7-lock`, the set's version with a trailer, the
  set itself being unchanged.
- The `## Waiting` conditions are unmet, `vc-x1 closed` not landed and jj-lib offering no remote
  query, so nothing promotes.

#### Solution

`custom.md` carries the lock as its first line, and the plan for the rest is first in `## Todo`.

- A session probes `.agent-running` at acquaint before anything else and holds it exclusive
  with a background command when it is free.
- A session that finds it held replies "Another session holds `.agent-running`, stopping." and
  runs no further command.
- The lock file is in `.gitignore`.
- The Todo entry describes the exclusive lock and the probe, and plans `.vc-x1-running`, a lock
  `vc-x1` takes for every run.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate` passes. Passed, on the pushed work.
- A fresh session started in this workspace while another holds the lock replies "Another
  session holds `.agent-running`, stopping." and its transcript shows the probe as its only
  shell command. Passed, before the push and not run again after it, wink's call: the session
  met the wording that was pushed, `custom.md` not having changed since.

#### Ladder

- docs: a session takes the workspace lock at acquaint (done)

#### Closing

Close-out shape: one commit, the closing folded into the work commit.

- A rule an agent follows is tested by the transcript of a session that meets it cold.
  - The line took four wordings, and each fault showed only in a transcript: a fetch beside the
    lock, a `pgrep`, a `ps` after a reply that read as correct.
  - A session already open tests nothing, having the old wording in mind.
- A count that binds is taken before the name is published.
  - The title was offered at 53 characters and its slug pushed as the bookmark before the count
    was made.
- A validation's verdict was lost once to its own output.
  - The run printed more than the session's tool shows, the last line with it, and it was run
    again into a file under `tmp/`, where the exit status says pass or fail.

# References

to make a second one, and `vc-x1 push` can only make a new commit on each side. The cycle
**docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md** did it by hand: a `jj squash`, a `jj describe`
with a trailer written by hand, and then the push.

  and the work commit gains a trailer for it. One work commit then names every agent-repo commit
  made for it.

session holds for as long as it runs. Its plan left open whether the
lock was to be a counter, the `flock`, or a counter guarded by one,
and whether the holder dies with its session was untested.

    the lock is the `flock` alone and there is no counter.

  - The link is dropped.
* The plan for the lock `vc-x1` is to take for each of its runs sat
  inside the session lock's entry.
  - It is an entry of its own, first in `## Todo`, and carries what
    the session lock leaves to be done.

111	## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do
112	
113	`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
114	and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
115	of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
116	([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
117	repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:
118	
119	- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
120	  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
121	  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
122	- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
123	  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
124	  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
125	- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
126	  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
127	- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
128	  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
129	    bookmark the work-repo is on.
130	  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
131	    the wrong remote ref.
132	- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.
133	  - The agent keeps writing session data while the command runs, so its own record lands after
134	    the squash.
135	  - Session data is append-only, so a re-run never conflicts.
136	  - A single pass is never guaranteed to leave `@` empty.
137	
138	A late work-repo tweak after the push (a forgotten edit) needs `jj squash --ignore-immutable` and a
139	re-push, which is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push.
140	
141	## Re-describing: coordinate first, and keep the trailer
142	
143	**Never `jj describe` a commit that is already published or already carries trailers without
144	coordinating with everyone involved first**
145	([why](rationale.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)). It is a history rewrite,
146	and it silently drops the cross-repo link. Describing a fresh local commit that has never been
147	described and carries no trailers is authoring a message rather than rewriting one, and is not
148	covered. That is a [local
149	ladder](../AGENTS.md#local-ladders)'s scratch describe.
150	
151	When a re-describe is agreed, copy any `ochid:` trailers into the new body by hand (the "don't
152	hand-write trailers" rule covers push authoring a message from scratch, not preserving one already
153	stamped). Hit at a coordinated amend (2026-07-29), where the trailer survived only that way.
154	`vc-x1 fix-desc` repairs a dropped one by title match.
155	
156	## Cycle bookmarks: create and land
157	
158	The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark). That section
159	holds the rule and when it applies, and this one holds the commands
160	([why](rationale.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
161	
162	**Create**, at the cycle's opening, with the bookmark named by the cycle title's slug (the anchor
163	algorithm in [Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links), so the block's title heading
164	and the bookmark derive from one bare title):
165	
166	- `jj git push --named <bookmark>=@- -R .` is the common case: it creates the bookmark at the last
167	  committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
168	- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
169	  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line. Otherwise the bookmark
170	  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.
171	- `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <rev> -R .` creates it without publishing, for a line that is not
172	  ready to be seen.
173	
174	**Land**, once the close-out is approved: the sequence that makes the cycle permanent. Every
175	`jj git push` in it is a push under [Approval per push](../AGENTS.md#before-any-push) and [Hard
176	stop after the final push](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push), its own approval, the
177	closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
178	rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):
179	
180	1. Restore the plain name, when the project renamed ([Dev artifact
181	   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
182	   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
183	   (`@` sits directly above it).
184	2. Reshape per the recorded choice: trapezoid runs the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe),
185	   keep separate needs nothing. A single-step cycle has no choice recorded and its one commit lands
186	   as it is.
187	3. Fast-forward: `jj bookmark set main -r <closeout> -R .`, then `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.
188	   This push publishes the reshaped commit, so the topic bookmark itself is never re-pushed.
189	4. Install: promote the artifact from `main`, the cycle's last act, run when nothing can enter the
190	   cycle anymore.
191	5. Delete the bookmark, locally and remotely: `jj bookmark delete <bookmark>`, then
192	   `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark>` ([Bookmark per
193	   cycle](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). The long-lived case below gets the same
194	   disposal once fully merged.
195	
196	- The fast-forward needs no `--allow-backwards`. Needing it means the bookmark is not a descendant
197	  of `main`, and the situation wants a look, not a flag.
198	- Landing is the moment the cycle's commits become permanent. No record cites their SHAs
199	  ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)): the landed commits are the record.
200	
201	**Reshape**, while the bookmark is a draft ([Cycles run on a
202	bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)):
203	
204	- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
205	  `jj describe`, so [No re-describe without
206	  coordinating](#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer) stays intact.
207	- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
208	- **Exceptions**, named and moved past: the bookmark has already landed, another branch is stacked
209	  on it, or the ladder is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.
210	
211	## Long-lived bookmarks: merge-only by default, deletable once merged
212	
213	A long-lived bookmark (a program line pushed rung by rung across cycles) is not a cycle bookmark: it
214	carries published history, and the discipline protects that history while the bookmark is its only
215	holder.
216	
217	- conflicts with `main` are resolved in merge commits, never by rewriting published rungs
218	- a rebase is never required for correctness: it is a linearity preference
219	- coordinated rebases stay available (the bar is on unilateral rewrites, not rewrites), at the known
220	  cost of staling the git-SHA citations in the records. Chids and ochid trailers survive a rebase
221	- once the bookmark's history is fully merged into `main` the bookmark is redundant and is deleted,
222	  locally and remotely
223	
224	The contrast with a cycle bookmark is the whole point: that one is a draft and may be rewritten
225	freely until it lands (see [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)), this
226	one is published and may not. Refined 2026-08-03 from the earlier "treated as permanent, never
227	rebased" wording, after a fully merged long-lived bookmark was deleted without loss.
228	
229	## Close-out shapes
230	
231	The two shapes a ladder can land in, chosen by the user and recorded at close-out, executed at
232	[Land](#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land) ([Close-out](../AGENTS.md#close-out)). A single-step cycle
233	is one commit and lands as it is:
234	
235	- **trapezoid**, the current default: a merge commit whose first parent is the trunk and whose
236	  second is the ladder, so `git log --first-parent` reads one commit per cycle while every rung
237	  stays reachable. Reshaped at Land by the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe) and published
238	  by the landing fast-forward itself.
239	- **keep separate**, one commit per rung on `main`, when the decomposition itself is informative.
240	
241	Squash is not a shape: each rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, a squash keeps one and drops the
242	rest, and every agent-repo commit that pointed at a dropped rung is left dangling ([Cycle
243	shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).
244	
245	**Preview before choosing.** The cycle's net change is the tree diff from `<base>` to the tip,
246	whatever shape the commits between are in: `jj diff --from <base> --to <tip>`, or the gitk range
247	described in [Read a change in gitk at full context](#read-a-change-in-gitk-at-full-context). The
248	trapezoid keeps each rung reachable while `git log --first-parent` shows this net diff once landed,
249	and keep separate shows the rungs themselves. The choice is made on what `main` will carry.

## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do

`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
    bookmark the work-repo is on.
  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
    the wrong remote ref.
- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.
  - The agent keeps writing session data while the command runs, so its own record lands after
    the squash.
  - Session data is append-only, so a re-run never conflicts.
  - A single pass is never guaranteed to leave `@` empty.

A late work-repo tweak after the push (a forgotten edit) needs `jj squash --ignore-immutable` and a
re-push, which is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push.

## Re-describing: coordinate first, and keep the trailer

**Never `jj describe` a commit that is already published or already carries trailers without
coordinating with everyone involved first**
([why](rationale.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)). It is a history rewrite,
and it silently drops the cross-repo link. Describing a fresh local commit that has never been
described and carries no trailers is authoring a message rather than rewriting one, and is not
covered. That is a [local
ladder](../AGENTS.md#local-ladders)'s scratch describe.

When a re-describe is agreed, copy any `ochid:` trailers into the new body by hand (the "don't
hand-write trailers" rule covers push authoring a message from scratch, not preserving one already
stamped). Hit at a coordinated amend (2026-07-29), where the trailer survived only that way.
`vc-x1 fix-desc` repairs a dropped one by title match.

## Cycle bookmarks: create and land

The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark). That section
holds the rule and when it applies, and this one holds the commands
([why](rationale.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).

**Create**, at the cycle's opening, with the bookmark named by the cycle title's slug (the anchor
algorithm in [Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links), so the block's title heading
and the bookmark derive from one bare title):

- `jj git push --named <bookmark>=@- -R .` is the common case: it creates the bookmark at the last
  committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line. Otherwise the bookmark
  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.
- `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <rev> -R .` creates it without publishing, for a line that is not
  ready to be seen.

**Land**, once the close-out is approved: the sequence that makes the cycle permanent. Every
`jj git push` in it is a push under [Approval per push](../AGENTS.md#before-any-push) and [Hard
stop after the final push](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push), its own approval, the
closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):

1. Restore the plain name, when the project renamed ([Dev artifact
   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
   (`@` sits directly above it).
2. Reshape per the recorded choice: trapezoid runs the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe),
   keep separate needs nothing. A single-step cycle has no choice recorded and its one commit lands
   as it is.
3. Fast-forward: `jj bookmark set main -r <closeout> -R .`, then `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.
   This push publishes the reshaped commit, so the topic bookmark itself is never re-pushed.
4. Install: promote the artifact from `main`, the cycle's last act, run when nothing can enter the
   cycle anymore.
5. Delete the bookmark, locally and remotely: `jj bookmark delete <bookmark>`, then
   `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark>` ([Bookmark per
   cycle](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). The long-lived case below gets the same
   disposal once fully merged.

- The fast-forward needs no `--allow-backwards`. Needing it means the bookmark is not a descendant
  of `main`, and the situation wants a look, not a flag.
- Landing is the moment the cycle's commits become permanent. No record cites their SHAs
  ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)): the landed commits are the record.

**Reshape**, while the bookmark is a draft ([Cycles run on a
bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)):

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so [No re-describe without
  coordinating](#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer) stays intact.
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions**, named and moved past: the bookmark has already landed, another branch is stacked
  on it, or the ladder is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

## Long-lived bookmarks: merge-only by default, deletable once merged

A long-lived bookmark (a program line pushed rung by rung across cycles) is not a cycle bookmark: it
carries published history, and the discipline protects that history while the bookmark is its only
holder.

- conflicts with `main` are resolved in merge commits, never by rewriting published rungs
- a rebase is never required for correctness: it is a linearity preference
- coordinated rebases stay available (the bar is on unilateral rewrites, not rewrites), at the known
  cost of staling the git-SHA citations in the records. Chids and ochid trailers survive a rebase
- once the bookmark's history is fully merged into `main` the bookmark is redundant and is deleted,
  locally and remotely

The contrast with a cycle bookmark is the whole point: that one is a draft and may be rewritten
freely until it lands (see [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)), this
one is published and may not. Refined 2026-08-03 from the earlier "treated as permanent, never
rebased" wording, after a fully merged long-lived bookmark was deleted without loss.

## Close-out shapes

The two shapes a ladder can land in, chosen by the user and recorded at close-out, executed at
[Land](#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land) ([Close-out](../AGENTS.md#close-out)). A single-step cycle
is one commit and lands as it is:

- **trapezoid**, the current default: a merge commit whose first parent is the trunk and whose
  second is the ladder, so `git log --first-parent` reads one commit per cycle while every rung
  stays reachable. Reshaped at Land by the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe) and published
  by the landing fast-forward itself.
- **keep separate**, one commit per rung on `main`, when the decomposition itself is informative.

Squash is not a shape: each rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, a squash keeps one and drops the
rest, and every agent-repo commit that pointed at a dropped rung is left dangling ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

**Preview before choosing.** The cycle's net change is the tree diff from `<base>` to the tip,
whatever shape the commits between are in: `jj diff --from <base> --to <tip>`, or the gitk range
described in [Read a change in gitk at full context](#read-a-change-in-gitk-at-full-context). The
trapezoid keeps each rung reachable while `git log --first-parent` shows this net diff once landed,
and keep separate shows the rungs themselves. The choice is made on what `main` will carry.

87	### Bullet form
88	
89	A bullet is a full sentence, capitalized and ending in a period or question mark, unless the list
90	is a plain list of things (files, names, options), which takes neither. A list is all one or all
91	the other. A sentence never opens with a lower-case name (`squash-push`, `rationale.md`), it is
92	recast so the name is not the first word.
93	
94	### Line widths
95	
96	Every width number lives here and nowhere else: the other files and sections link here rather than
97	restating one, so a change is a single edit and the copies cannot drift. Consolidated 2026-08-09,
98	when the body width moved and the restatements had to be hunted.
99	
100	- **Prose**, all durable text: wrap at <=100 cols, bullet continuations indented two spaces.
101	- **Source**, doc comments and inline comments included: <=100 cols, which is rustfmt's default
102	  `max_width` (enforcement notes in [code.md](code.md#line-width)).
103	- **Commit titles**: <=50 chars.
104	- **Commit bodies**: <=75 cols, the Linux kernel patch standard. It replaced git's older 72
105	  convention here 2026-08-09, and published bodies keep the wrap they shipped with.
106	
107	The widths are wrap defaults, not absolutes (the title cap excepted). Existing text re-wraps when
108	touched, no mass sweeps. Write to the full width: wrap near the limit rather than imitating the
109	narrow wrap of older text, and a line that reads better long stays long (an URL, a literal report
110	row, indented code in a comment).
111	
112	### Problem-first shape
113	
114	`## In Progress` cycle blocks, `## Todo` entries, and commit bodies use a sharper form of the same
115	shape: a problem, then how it is answered, then the steps that get there.
116	
117	- **Problem statement** (the why): one or two sentences. Don't pad with intent, don't restate what
118	  follows it.
119	- **Solution statement** (the what/how): what is done about the problem, in broad terms, answering
120	  whatever question the problem statement raises. Surface-specific rules are in [Bullet content
121	  differs by surface](#prose-form) above.
122	- **Plan bullets** (the what/when), the steps. Formality differs by surface:
123	  - In Progress: a committed ladder, one step per commit. See [Conventional-commit
124	    shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit) for the per-step title + `(current)` /
125	    `(done)` form.
126	  - Todo entries: rough informal bullets, no numbering, formalized only when the entry is picked up
127	    into a cycle.
128	
129	**Timing decides whether the solution statement is provisional, not whether it is written.** A cycle
130	writes one at Preparation, before the work, and revises it as steps land. The close-out's commit
131	body carries the final one. A `## Todo` entry's is provisional in the same way. Only a commit body's
132	is settled, because a commit is finished by the time it has one. The earlier rule here said a plan
133	was for work not yet done and a solution for work that is, which left a cycle unable to say at its
134	opening what it intended to do.
135	
136	### Commit-body form
137	
138	The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is the [Problem-first
139	shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
140	problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
141	bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
142	statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.
143	
144	- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
145	  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
146	  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
147	  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
148	  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
149	- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
150	  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
151	  to be more than one commit.
152	- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
153	  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
154	  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
155	- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
156	  form, the general form at its smallest.
157	- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
158	  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
159	  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.
160	
161	**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
162	pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
163	typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
164	read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
165	flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
166	a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.
167	
168	Unchanged by this: no version in title or body, no file list, no deliberation, titles per
169	[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit).
170	
171	### Semicolons

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as

total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### docs: the session lock is settled as flock

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) The Todo as it was picked, **The lock a running agent holds**, less
its plan for `.vc-x1-running`, which stays in `## Todo` as an entry of its own. The file is
`.agent-running` at the workspace root, in `.gitignore`. It is a mutex a running agent holds, one
session per workspace, and a second session that finds it held refuses to work. The entry ended
on an open line: whether the lock is a counter, the `flock`, or a counter guarded by one.

- Wink's first design: the file holds a counter, a session adds one and takes one away, and the
  file is deleted at 0.
  - The update is a read, change, and write that two sessions starting together can interleave,
    so it wants a guard.
  - A session that dies never takes its one away, and a number does not say which holder is dead.
- Linux's advisory lock, `flock`, answers both: the kernel releases it when its holder exits or
  dies. The file then has no contents and is never deleted.
  - The first form was shared: each session held it shared, and rename and delete asked for it
    exclusive without waiting. A second session then started as freely as the first.
  - Wink's call, 2026-10-11: one session per workspace. The session holds it exclusive and asks
    without waiting, so a second session's request fails at once instead of queueing.
  - It is advisory: it binds the processes that ask. Claude Code itself still starts, and the
    refusal is the agent's, by the `custom.md` line.
  - The lock lasts as long as the process holding it, and an agent's commands each exit at once,
    so a session needs one process that lives exactly as long as it does.
- The experiment: the agent takes the lock at acquaint, by a line in this project's `custom.md`,
  which [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) already reads and acts on.
  - The holder is a background command the agent starts, `flock -xn .agent-running sleep
    infinity`, so there is no release for the agent to forget.
  - A foreground probe comes first, `flock -xn .agent-running true`, since a background command
    reports its failure seconds later, after the session has moved on.
  - A refusal is one fixed sentence, so the session offers no way around the lock.
  - The check is `flock -xn .agent-running true` from another terminal: it fails while a session
    is open and succeeds after.
- What the experiment was to find out: whether the holder dies with its session, what a resumed
  session does, what a reacquaint does in a session that no longer remembers its holder, how an
  edit to the line reaches a session already open, and how rename and delete check.

#### Deliberation

- The lock is the `flock`, exclusive, and no counter, wink's call once the tests were in.
  - Every way a session ends releases it, so nothing is left for a counter to count.
  - The tests came before the cycle was opened, wink's call, each of them ending the session
    that would have reported it.
- The holder dies with its session, however the session ends.
  - A clean exit: a session was ended with `/exit`, and the next session's probe succeeded.
    Claude Code asks before that exit, the holder being a background command still running, and
    exiting anyway kills it. The question is one more key at every exit.
  - A crash: wink's check from a plain terminal exited 1 with a session open, Claude Code was
    killed with `kill -9`, and the check exited 0 twenty seconds later.
  - A closed terminal: the check exited 1 with the session open and 0 after its terminal
    window was closed.
  - A power loss: wink's pull-the-plug test, 2026-10-11, with a session open. With the machine
    back up the check exited 0, `.agent-running` was still there and empty, and `vc-x1 sync` and
    `vc-x1 st -s both` found both repos up to date and clean.
  - Each session ran its commands in Claude Code's sandbox. One run outside it is untested, and
    we think it is the same, the kernel releasing a lock when the last process holding it dies.
- A resumed session holds no lock, and the line now tells it to take one.
  - The session the closed terminal ended was resumed with `claude --resume`, and the check
    from a plain terminal still exited 0.
  - Claude Code tells the resumed session that its holder was stopped when the earlier process
    exited, and starts nothing in its place.
  - The line as it was gave that case the refusal sentence and the stop, the holder having
    exited, and the sentence would have been untrue, no other session holding the lock.
  - The session ran no command until wink said to take the lock again.
  - "If that command ever exits" became "exits while the session runs", so the two cases do not
    read as one.
- The probe run by the session that holds the lock exits 1, confirmed by running it.
  - A reacquaint in a session that no longer remembers its holder would read that as another
    session and stop. The line's "a session that already holds one does neither" is all that
    stands against it, and the case goes to the `.vc-x1-running` entry with the hook command.
- The link at the end of the lock line is dropped, the entry it named being this record.
- The `.vc-x1-running` plan is an entry of its own, first in `## Todo`, wink's call.

    proposal of the lock to the set.

    holds.

    landmark `docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md` says, the record kept in this file

  - The bend covers this cycle's two pushes and their shape. Land takes its own go.

  approved by wink at the opening.
- The `## Waiting` conditions are unmet, `vc-x1 closed` not landed and jj-lib offering no remote
  query, so nothing promotes.

Provisional: the session lock is recorded as finished, and what is left is planned elsewhere.

- The lock line in `custom.md` loses its link and gains the resumed session's case.
- The Todo entry becomes this record, with the four results and `flock`, exclusive, as the

# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as
the closing rung's last edit, with the cycle title as the row's label. `rationale.md` is out of the
total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

`vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides the per-file table, a new leftmost column in
and the oldest out. It is dry-run by default and `--no-dry-run` writes the file, `--label=TEXT`
names a column the set's version file cannot, and the `## Counts` row above stays a hand's work,
since its note is prose.

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### docs: the session lock is settled as flock

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) The Todo as it was picked, **The lock a running agent holds**, less
its plan for `.vc-x1-running`, which stays in `## Todo` as an entry of its own. The file is
`.agent-running` at the workspace root, in `.gitignore`. It is a mutex a running agent holds, one
session per workspace, and a second session that finds it held refuses to work. The entry ended
on an open line: whether the lock is a counter, the `flock`, or a counter guarded by one.

- Wink's first design: the file holds a counter, a session adds one and takes one away, and the
  file is deleted at 0.
  - The update is a read, change, and write that two sessions starting together can interleave,
    so it wants a guard.
  - A session that dies never takes its one away, and a number does not say which holder is dead.
- Linux's advisory lock, `flock`, answers both: the kernel releases it when its holder exits or
  dies. The file then has no contents and is never deleted.
  - The first form was shared: each session held it shared, and rename and delete asked for it
    exclusive without waiting. A second session then started as freely as the first.
  - Wink's call, 2026-10-11: one session per workspace. The session holds it exclusive and asks
    without waiting, so a second session's request fails at once instead of queueing.
  - It is advisory: it binds the processes that ask. Claude Code itself still starts, and the
    refusal is the agent's, by the `custom.md` line.
  - The lock lasts as long as the process holding it, and an agent's commands each exit at once,
    so a session needs one process that lives exactly as long as it does.
- The experiment: the agent takes the lock at acquaint, by a line in this project's `custom.md`,
  which [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) already reads and acts on.
  - The holder is a background command the agent starts, `flock -xn .agent-running sleep
    infinity`, so there is no release for the agent to forget.
  - A foreground probe comes first, `flock -xn .agent-running true`, since a background command
    reports its failure seconds later, after the session has moved on.
  - A refusal is one fixed sentence, so the session offers no way around the lock.
  - The check is `flock -xn .agent-running true` from another terminal: it fails while a session
    is open and succeeds after.
- What the experiment was to find out: whether the holder dies with its session, what a resumed
  session does, what a reacquaint does in a session that no longer remembers its holder, how an
  edit to the line reaches a session already open, and how rename and delete check.

#### Deliberation

- The lock is the `flock`, exclusive, and no counter, wink's call once the tests were in.
  - Every way a session ends releases it, so nothing is left for a counter to count.
  - The tests came before the cycle was opened, wink's call, each of them ending the session
    that would have reported it.
- The holder dies with its session, however the session ends.
  - A clean exit: a session was ended with `/exit`, and the next session's probe succeeded.
    Claude Code asks before that exit, the holder being a background command still running, and
    exiting anyway kills it. The question is one more key at every exit.
  - A crash: wink's check from a plain terminal exited 1 with a session open, Claude Code was
    killed with `kill -9`, and the check exited 0 twenty seconds later.
  - A closed terminal: the check exited 1 with the session open and 0 after its terminal
    window was closed.
  - A power loss: wink's pull-the-plug test, 2026-10-11, with a session open. With the machine
    back up the check exited 0, `.agent-running` was still there and empty, and `vc-x1 sync` and
    `vc-x1 st -s both` found both repos up to date and clean.
  - Each session ran its commands in Claude Code's sandbox. One run outside it is untested, and
    we think it is the same, the kernel releasing a lock when the last process holding it dies.
- A resumed session holds no lock, and the line now tells it to take one.
  - The session the closed terminal ended was resumed with `claude --resume`, and the check
    from a plain terminal still exited 0.
  - Claude Code tells the resumed session that its holder was stopped when the earlier process
    exited, and starts nothing in its place.
  - The line as it was gave that case the refusal sentence and the stop, the holder having
    exited, and the sentence would have been untrue, no other session holding the lock.
  - The session ran no command until wink said to take the lock again.
  - "If that command ever exits" became "exits while the session runs", so the two cases do not
    read as one.
- The probe run by the session that holds the lock exits 1, confirmed by running it.
  - A reacquaint in a session that no longer remembers its holder would read that as another
    session and stop. The line's "a session that already holds one does neither" is all that
    stands against it, and the case goes to the `.vc-x1-running` entry with the hook command.
- The link at the end of the lock line is dropped, the entry it named being this record.
- The `.vc-x1-running` plan is an entry of its own, first in `## Todo`, wink's call.
  - It takes what the session lock leaves: the hook command, the reacquaint cases, and the
    proposal of the lock to the set.
  - It answers how rename and delete check, the process that asks being the process that
    holds.
- The cycle is two stages and one work commit, wink's call, as the last two cycles ran.
  - It bends [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape), [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record),
    [Opening](AGENTS.md#opening), and [Close-out](AGENTS.md#close-out) as the record in the
    landmark `docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md` says, the record kept in this file
    included.
  - The fold of the closing into the work commit is by hand again, `push --amend` not being
    written, and is a coordinated re-describe with one trailer written by hand.
  - The bend covers this cycle's two pushes and their shape. Land takes its own go.
- The title was counted before the bookmark was published, 42 characters, and both were
  approved by wink at the opening.
- The `## Waiting` conditions are unmet, `vc-x1 closed` not landed and jj-lib offering no remote
  query, so nothing promotes.

#### Solution

The session lock is the `flock`, exclusive, with no counter, and what is left is planned in
`## Todo`.

- The lock line in `custom.md` lost its link and gained the resumed session's case.
- The Todo entry became this record, with its results and `flock`, exclusive, as the answer to
  its open line.
- The `.vc-x1-running` plan stands alone as the first entry in `## Todo`, and carries what the
  session lock leaves.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate` passes. Passed, on the pushed work and again on the closing.
- A session that met the new line cold takes the lock again when resumed: a fresh session is
  started and acquaints, its terminal is closed, it is resumed and sent one message, and its
  transcript shows the probe and the holder as its first two commands. The check from a plain
  terminal then exits 1. Not run, wink's call, to close the cycle the day it opened.
  - The closing session met the line cold at a fresh acquaint, and the probe and the holder
    were its first two commands. That is the line's acquaint case and says nothing of the
    resumed one.
  - The run is a line in the Todo entry [vc-x1 takes a lock of its own for every
    run](TODO.md#vc-x1-takes-a-lock-of-its-own-for-every-run).

#### Ladder

- docs: the session lock is settled as flock (done)

#### Closing

Close-out shape: one commit, the closing folded into the work commit.

- The power loss was tested after the work was pushed, and its result is in the Deliberation
  with the other three ways a session ends.
- The parked proposal was reviewed in the closing session and stays parked, wink's call.
  - Its Todo entry, [agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8](TODO.md#agent-filesproposal-v028), has
    what the review settled: a look at acquaint, a sync at the opening, and a sync at Land.
- The size table's new column is labelled `v0.2.7-flock`, the set itself being unchanged.

# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as
the closing rung's last edit, with the cycle title as the row's label. `rationale.md` is out of the
total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

`vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides the per-file table, a new leftmost column in
and the oldest out. It is dry-run by default and `--no-dry-run` writes the file, `--label=TEXT`
names a column the set's version file cannot, and the `## Counts` row above stays a hand's work,
since its note is prose.

  does not repeat is a finding, reported and given a Todo entry.
